meeting_header:
Date: 2027-06-23
Time: 15:00 - 15:52 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood CSM), Tom Reynolds (VP Eng, SageBridge), Sara Holt (Head of MLOps), Dr. Angela Park (Dir Clinical Data), Jamal Reed (DevOps), Maya Li (PM)
summary: Onboarding kickoff for SageBridge Health. Introductions and success criteria, review of deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC), SSO and security requirements, data residency and audit log discussions. Agreed next steps: share onboarding docs, schedule infra sizing and benchmark, start SSO setup. Customer emphasized latency targets for clinical inference and strict audit requirements.
topics: Security: SOC2, SAML/SSO, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
00:00 Laura Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Laura from Redwood, i'm the AE for SageBridge. quick round robin?
00:05 Tom Reynolds: yea Tom here, VP Eng at SageBridge. nice to meet you.
00:09 Miguel Ortiz: miguel, solutions engineer, i'll own the technical side of onboarding and benchmarks.
00:13 Priya Singh: priya, customer success, i'll coordinate milestones and runbooks.
00:18 Sara Holt: sara - head of mops, i'll be point on infra and security.
00:22 Dr. Angela Park: angela - clinical data, interested in model accuracy and auditability.
00:27 Jamal Reed: jamal, devops.
00:30 Laura Chen: great, thanks. quick agenda — align on success criteria, discuss which deployment to start with, auth/networking, benchmarks and pilot. any additions?
00:40 Maya Li: just add timeline — we want a pilot in july if possible.
00:44 Laura Chen: noted. tom, priya mentioned y'all want a july pilot? what's the priority and internal stakeholders?
00:51 Tom Reynolds: yeah priority high. execs want to see clinical triage assistant in pilot by mid july. stakeholders are product, clinical, security. budget approved for dedicated or private depending on risk.
01:05 Laura Chen: ok that's helpful. can you share high level qps and latency SLOs?
01:10 Sara Holt: looking for avg p95 latency under 400ms for short chat flows, and up to 1s for longer context. qps around 25 steady with spikes to 75 during peak.
01:22 Miguel Ortiz: that's doable; we'll run a sizing exercise. dedicated nodes typically can hit that with batching tweaks, and private can too depending on infra.
01:30 Dr. Angela Park: also need strict audit logs and data residency — PHI may be in prompts, so encryption and KMS are musts.
01:38 Priya Singh: we have SOC2 and enterprise on our compliance matrix; we can walk through SAML + KMS options.
01:43 Laura Chen: quick note — recommended onboarding path: start with Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity for pilot (predictable), use private deployment later for full production if needed. but we can map to your risk posture.
01:55 Tom Reynolds: what are the tradeoffs — cost vs latency vs ops?
01:58 Miguel Ortiz: simple: hosted is fastest to start but not acceptable for PHI in your case; dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower ops burden; private gives you network isolation and KMS control but needs infra. Cost goes up with isolation.
02:12 Jamal Reed: we prefer VPC/private for PHI; we can provision but need clear infra checklist.
02:18 Miguel Ortiz: understood. we'll send an infra checklist, VPC peering guidance, and required firewall rules.
02:25 Laura Chen: security — sara can you confirm required certifications?
02:28 Sara Holt: SOC2 type II required; we might request SOC report and pen test summary. also SAML SSO with Okta.
02:36 Laura Chen: we can provide SOC2 report and SSO integration guide. we also have audit log retention settings and optionally ship logs to your SIEM.
02:45 Dr. Angela Park: log immutability and chain of custody are important — can we get a sample audit log format?
02:50 Miguel Ortiz: yes we'll share sample logs and the event schema. note transcriptions sometimes anonymize PII so we can show patterns.
03:00 Tom Reynolds: on model behavior — we have concerns about hallucinations in clinical context. what's Redwood's approach to quality monitoring?
03:07 Priya Singh: we have quality monitoring tied to prompt sets and evals, can alert on regressions and rollback to previous model versions. we'll include a demo in the pilot.
03:16 Sara Holt: do you support our own models or only Redwood-curated ones?
03:20 Miguel Ortiz: both — you can bring a custom model image for private or run an open model from our catalog. for production, we recommend a validated version and we can help pin versions for canary rollouts.
03:31 Maya Li: for pilot scope, we only need basic routing + model for triage plus logging and SSO. if we can prove latency and quality, we'll expand.
03:39 Laura Chen: timeline check: priya?
03:42 Priya Singh: ok milestones: onboarding docs + SSO guides shared by 6/25, infra sizing + benchmark run the week of 6/28, SSO integration and test week of 7/5, pilot start target 7/12. we'll sync weekly. sound realistic?
03:58 Tom Reynolds: yes that works.
04:01 Miguel Ortiz: i'll need network contacts and sample prompt sets to simulate load. can we get those?
04:06 Sara Holt: jamal will provide network contacts, sara to send prompts by 6/29.
04:12 Jamal Reed: yep i'll share vpc and firewall owner contact.
04:15 Laura Chen: great. now quick technical questions — miguel can you talk about KV cache and batching impact?
04:22 Miguel Ortiz: sure. for clinical triage, session sticks matter; KV cache reduces repeated context recomputation significantly. batching helps throughput but increases tail latency a bit. we'll tune continuous batching and prefix caching to meet the p95 400ms. approximate approach: smaller batch sizes for low latency flows, larger for throughput jobs. quant profiles can reduce cost if model tolerates it.
04:45 Dr. Angela Park: do you offer quantization recommendations?
04:47 Miguel Ortiz: yes, Redwood Optimize provides quantization guidance per workload; we'll include recommended quant profiles in the benchmark spreadsheet.
04:54 Tom Reynolds: audit and compliance again — who holds the logs? how long retained?
04:58 Laura Chen: you can configure retention; by default enterprise plan has 90 days but can extend. for PHI customers we recommend exporting to your SIEM or using private deployment with your KMS and retention policies.
05:12 Sara Holt: ok please include export options and KMS flow.
05:16 Priya Singh: noted. I'll add runbook steps for exporting logs to your S3/SIEM.
05:21 Maya Li: any blockers around Okta SAML?
05:24 Miguel Ortiz: no, we support Okta SAML out of the box; we'll send a step-by-step SSO setup doc. sometimes metadata requires a quick reformat.
05:33 Tom Reynolds: curious about fallback behavior if dedicated capacity is saturated — automatic fallback to hosted?
05:38 Miguel Ortiz: yes you can configure smart routing and fallback policies: route to dedicated, fallback to a lower-capacity variant or to hosted with reduced context. we'll recommend safe fallbacks for production.
05:51 Laura Chen: wrapping up, recap and owners: Laura will send onboarding checklist and pricing; Miguel sends infra checklist and benchmarking spreadsheet + schedules sizing call; Priya creates the CS project and invites stakeholders. Tom/Jamal/Sara provide network contacts and prompt sets. next sync in one week, and benchmark week of 6/28.
06:12 Tom Reynolds: thanks everyone, excited to get started.
06:16 Laura Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and meeting invites.
06:19 End of recording (52 minutes)
